Performers
Marine Chamber Orchestra, United States Marine Band (orchestra), Major Michelle A. Rakers (conductor) Documented

Commons gives the conductor as Major Michelle Rakers; the programme prints Major Michelle A. Rakers. No roster of individual players is published in the consulted sources. The wide shot in this video’s thumbnail shows a harpsichord at stage left, strings with a double bass and a bassoon; a trumpet is visible in the Hornpipe video, and no frame shows horns or oboes. Which sections play in each of the three passes is not established: an independent look at the official video reports upper-string players resting at about 0:34, where the printed score gives them notes, so the recording is not assumed to follow the printed parts. No orchestra view is authored for this movement for that reason.

[1] [4] [2]
Work version
Performing edition not identified. The movement number (15 of the three suites) and the structure heard (a four-bar and an eight-bar strain, each repeated, the whole air played three times) match the Hallische Händel-⁠Ausgabe text and its instruction “This Air to be played 3 times over”; no editor or continuo realisation is credited. Inferred, not documented

The programme and Commons name the work and movement numbers but no edition. The structure follows from the measured pauses and the Hallische Händel-⁠Ausgabe (Redlich, 1962), which prints 12 bars with repeat signs and the instruction on p. 53; IMSLP lists the movement as 12 bars played three times (36). The higher level of the third pass is a feature of this performance: the printed notes are the same for all three.

[4] [7] [8] [6]
Recorded
2017-01-29 Documented

Commons gives performance_date 2017-01-29; the programme prints Sunday, January 29, 2017 at 2:00 P.M.; the official video description repeats the date. The Handel group stands after the intermission in the programme. The Commons composition_date field, 1717-07-17, is the date of the documented first performance on the Thames, not a composition date.

Place
Rachel M. Schlesinger Concert Hall and Arts Center, Northern Virginia Community College, Alexandria Campus, Alexandria, Virginia, United States Documented

Commons says Schlesinger Concert Hall, Alexandria, VA; the programme gives the full name of the hall and campus.

[1] [4]
Label
Unknown Unknown

No record label is identified. The source is an official concert video on the Marine Band’s YouTube channel; the channel is not treated as a label, and no commercial release was found.

[1] [2]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

No transfer or mastering engineer is identified. The Commons file history shows the batch upload by the user Mysterymanblue (pattypan), which is an uploader credit, not an engineering credit.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is documented. The YouTube publication date (30 April 2018) and the Commons upload date (28 June 2021) are not session or transfer dates.

[1] [2]
Processing
Opus audio file (48 kHz, two channels, encoder Lavf58.29.100) listed on Commons with the Marine Band’s YouTube playlist as its source; Commons supplies an MP3 access derivative. Inferred, not documented

The file’s own metadata documents the Opus format and encoder. That the audio was taken from the official video’s sound track is inferred from the source field and from the matching title and duration (76 s); the processing chain is not described.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Handel (died 1759): the composition is in the public domain. Documented

Commons tags the composition PD-old-auto-expired (death year 1759). The performing edition is not identified; editorial copyright in a modern edition, if one was used, is separate from the sound recording.

[1]
Recording rights
Commons tags the performance and recording PD-USGov-⁠Military-⁠Marines: a work of a United States Marine or employee made as part of official duties, public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government. Documented

This is a U.S.-jurisdiction statement, not a claim of worldwide status. The programme carries a general notice that a performance may contain third-party material and should not be assumed to be public domain; no third-party material is identified in this performance of a composition from before 1759, but the notice is recorded here. The official Marine Band YouTube channel published the source video.

George Frideric Handel, Water Music, Suite No. 2 in D, HWV 349: IV. Bourrée. Marine Chamber Orchestra of the United States Marine Band, Major Michelle Rakers conducting; Rachel M. Schlesinger Concert Hall, Alexandria, Virginia, 29 January 2017. Audio via Wikimedia Commons from the official Marine Band concert video. U.S. federal-government work; public domain in the United States. Rights statement

  7. Händel, Wassermusik Suite II HWV 349, Hallische Händel-⁠Ausgabe IV/13, ed. Hans Ferdinand Redlich (Bärenreiter, 1962), via IMSLP #559922 — Printed p. 53 (movement 15, bars 1–⁠12): cut time with a one-note upbeat, repeat signs after bars 4 and 12, the instruction “This Air to be played 3 times over”, every section playing in every bar, bass figures 4–⁠3 in bar 11 and a final dotted minim. Consulted for bar numbering only; its copyright status in the United States is not established and it is not the stated score source of the orchestra view.. Accessed 2026-10-17.

Handel, The Celebrated Water-musick in score (London: Samuel Arnold, 1788) — Bibliothèque nationale de France scan on Wikimedia Commons — Printed pp. 49–⁠50 (Commons images 26–⁠27 of 30): the Bourrée in cut time for trumpets, horns, oboes, bassoon, strings and figured bass. Commons tags the scans PD-old-auto-expired, PD-France and PD-US-expired.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
